extracted.intended_audience: students and readers of philosophy, particularly those studying aesthetics and Schopenhauer
extracted.subtask_description: Schopenhauer's aesthetic theory: criteria for what counts as Art, Genius, and aesthetic perception — how art apprehends Ideas (adequate objectivity of the will) versus ordinary/scientific knowledge. Useful for evaluating artworks, genius, and modes of perception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Art reproduces eternal Ideas (adequate objectivity of the will)
rubrics_metrics.description: Art repeats or reproduces the eternal Ideas grasped through pure contemplation; its one source is the knowledge of Ideas and its one aim the communication of this knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Art isolates a particular thing out of the world's flux and makes it representative of the whole (the Idea). Depending on the material, this reproduction is sculpture, painting, poetry, or music. Examples and analogies: clouds, brooks, crystals show forces (Ideas) in different degrees; art picks the essential (Idea) and not the accidental forms. Anti-pattern: treating mere phenomenal relations or historical events as the final aim of art rather than as accidental manifestations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Art as a way of viewing things independent of the principle of sufficient reason
rubrics_metrics.description: Art's method is 'the way of viewing things independent of the principle of sufficient reason' in opposition to the rational/scientific method which traces relations, causes, time and place.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where science seeks relations and is always progressive and unsatisfied, art 'pauses' at a particular and attains its goal by revealing the Idea. The analogy: scientific view is a horizontal line of relations; art is a vertical line cutting it at a point. Use this to judge whether an approach or work is genuinely artistic (focuses on essence) or merely scientific/analytic (focuses on relations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Art's aim: communication of knowledge of Ideas
rubrics_metrics.description: The singular aim of art is to communicate knowledge of the Ideas (the eternal, essential forms of things) to others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess artworks by whether they convey an insight into the essential, timeless aspect of their subject rather than merely entertaining or recounting contingent events. Art 'halts' time and isolates a particular to represent the universal; it thereby attains its goal, unlike science which never reaches a final satisfaction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genius as capacity for pure, will-less contemplation
rubrics_metrics.description: Genius is the pre-eminent capacity for the pure contemplation that forgets the will: the power to lose one's individuality and remain the pure, will-less subject of knowledge long enough to apprehend Ideas and reproduce them in art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Genius is judged by (a) the ability to cease tracing relations (where, when, why) and instead attend wholly to the 'what'; (b) renouncing personal interests and aims; (c) sustaining pure perception to enable deliberate artistic reproduction. Scoring-note: duration and depth of such detached perception are central — sporadic imagination is insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pure aesthetic perception: losing self and ceasing to trace relations
rubrics_metrics.description: Aesthetic perception requires the subject to 'lose' himself — to cease being an individual guided by the will and to stop tracing where/when/why/how; instead the subject rests in fixed contemplation of the object and apprehends the Idea.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicators include forgetting individuality, absence of concern with utility or causation, and being occupied wholly by a single sensuous picture. This state makes time, place, causality meaningless for the perceiver and is the condition for Art and for the man of genius to apprehend Ideas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imagination is necessary but not sufficient for genius
rubrics_metrics.description: Extraordinary strength of imagination accompanies and is a necessary condition of genius because it extends the horizon beyond immediate perception, but imagination alone does not equal genius.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use imagination's role to distinguish: (a) genius uses imagination to reconstruct the Idea from imperfect particulars and to enlarge content; (b) the mere imaginative dreamer builds castles for egoistic gratification and lacks the capacity for pure contemplation. Anti-pattern: equating imaginative prolificity with artistic genius.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction between genius' imagination and dreamer's imagination
rubrics_metrics.description: An imaginary object can be apprehended either as a means to knowledge of Ideas (genius) or as gratification of the individual will and relations (dreamer); the former yields art, the latter produces fantasies/entertaining novels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate creative works by whether imagined content serves to reveal essential Ideas (genius) or merely constructs egotistic fancies and pleasurable scenarios (dreamer). Example: ordinary novels often cater to readers' imaginings of themselves in a hero's place and do not convey Ideas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Science treats phenomena and relations; art treats Ideas and essence
rubrics_metrics.description: Science, governed by the principle of sufficient reason, studies phenomena—their laws, connections, and relations in space and time—whereas art addresses that which is outside relations: the eternal, unchanging Ideas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When judging a work or inquiry, ask whether its subject-matter and method aim at uncovering causal relations (scientific) or at revealing the unchanging essence (artistic). Both have legitimate domains; misapplying one method to the other's aim is an error.

rubrics_metrics.name: Art 'pauses' the flow of time and isolates particulars as representatives of the universal
rubrics_metrics.description: Art takes a particular fleeting object out of the stream of the world's course and makes it representative of the whole; thereby time 'stops' and only the essential (Idea) remains.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether a work successfully renders a particular as emblematic of an eternal form. If the work remains immersed in temporal relations and contingency, it fails as high art according to this standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signs of a man of genius in appearance and temperament
rubrics_metrics.description: The man of genius is outwardly marked by a keen, steady, contemplative glance, a restlessness and aspiration unmet by present satisfactions, and awkwardness in pursuing ordinary life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these behavioral and physical signs as supplementary indicators of genius (not definitive proof). They accompany the inner capacity for prolonged disinterested contemplation: eagerness for lofty objects, dissatisfaction with ordinary life, and social awkwardness.
